walkthroughs.body_html: By 1492 Castile and Aragon had completed the Reconquista with the surrender of Granada. Portuguese exploration around Africa, the rediscovery of classical geography and improved navigation (caravels, astrolabes, magnetic compass) made transoceanic ventures plausible. Columbus, drawing on under-estimates of the earth's circumference, secured backing from Isabella and Ferdinand.

Sailing on 3 August 1492 with the Santa María, Pinta and Niña, Columbus reached landfall in the Bahamas on 12 October. He explored Hispaniola and Cuba, established a small garrison and returned to Spain. Subsequent voyages (1493, 1498, 1502) extended Spanish presence in the Caribbean and along the South American coast.

The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) split the non-European world between Spain and Portugal. Encomienda labour, forced conversion and epidemic disease devastated Indigenous populations. The voyages launched what historians call the Columbian Exchange, with vast biological, cultural and economic consequences.
